wedge: Standalone consumer data/content/alert products only: public-data alerts, directories, watchlists, update trackers, local reports and content+tool assets that serve ordinary consumers without B2B/admin or privileged platform dependence.
last_material_result: KILLED Apartment Maintenance Fee Anomaly Watch after the bounded demand/substitute test. Consumer pain is real: 2026 winter coverage reports residents surprised by sharply higher monthly fees and K-apt data showing nationwide January fees up year-over-year, driven especially by heating and individual-use charges. But the remaining action-layer wedge is not sufficiently distinct: Apartment-i already serves roughly 30,000 complexes / 12 million households and explicitly provides mobile bill notifications, itemized month-over-month deltas, utility-category analysis, and comparison against same-complex/same-size averages. App reviews also describe using prior-month and same-size comparisons to identify what changed. A public-data-only product would have weaker household-level data than this incumbent and no clear recurring distribution or monetization advantage. Generic comparison was already rejected, and both remaining wedges—'this month jumped' alert and 'why did it jump' explanation—are substantially covered by the incumbent. No build justified.
economics: KRW0 validation spend. Government data could remain free, but expected standalone contribution is now low: dominant free incumbent already owns bill notification + household-level item analysis + peer comparison, while a K-apt-only entrant would lack private household consumption detail. Ads/premium-alert economics would require acquiring users for functionality they can already get free, so expected value does not justify build/maintenance.
next_checkpoint: Next Lane C run: return to fresh genetic discovery in a materially different public-data consumer domain. Prefer information that is fragmented across official sources, changes often enough to reward alerts, and lacks a dominant free consumer app already combining notification + explanation + action.
recommendation: KILL Apartment Maintenance Fee Anomaly Watch and resume fresh discovery. Do not mutate it into generic apartment-fee comparison, household bill analysis, or payment/discount tooling.
